analysis:
Examined the head excerpts of EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (lines 526-1127), the EngineV2Bridge.swift doc-comment patch, and the BASE text. The submission patch excerpt is truncated. Per the visible range map, the PR adds a per-request `stopStringScope` parameter on the submit and submitTokenized paths (new around lines 63, 83, 136-138). For the native block engine it forces nil, so stops match over the whole output (about lines 325-329). Line 1073 passes `cbv2Request.stopStringScope` into `runPump`. The EngineV2Bridge.swift change is comment-only.

The visible head code covers shared-KV reservation, prefix-cache staging and release, first-content-deadline checks, atomic admission, retirement transfer, and pump startup. This section looks unchanged apart from line 1073. I found no new handling of plaintext or keys, no new disk artifacts, no new prefix-cache keys, and no change to the TTL or lookup-tag derivation, so T-041/TB-007 are unaffected. Cleanup paths (releasePreSubmitResources, abandonPrefixStaging, discardPrefixReadyReceipt, transferPreSubmitRetirement) still run on the error branches I could see.

The stop-scope value is a request-level behaviour control. Its origin (`ReasoningStopScope`) is not in the supplied evidence. The callers that compute it, the `runPump` stop matching, and the engine-side honouring of `stopStringScope` are not visible in this batch. Integration should check that a consumer cannot supply an arbitrary scope that causes stop strings to be skipped or applied incorrectly. Consumers are adversarial, but the effect is limited to the consumer's own output. I did not find a concrete security regression, so findings is empty. I recommend deeper review of the unseen portions of the patch, and of the callers and pump handling, because of the truncation.
